subject: GCP private offer — bundled addon surge credits + partner netback
messages:
From: Tim Jones <tim.jones@cobaltanalyics.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@cobaltanalyics.com; susan.kim@resellco.com
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: GCP private offer question — bundled addon + surge credits

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile on your GCP nodes looks promising. We're shaping a private offer for a pilot that bundles base inference tokens + two paid addons (hf-ops for streaming and an embeddings indexing add-on). Two asks from our procurement/reseller side:

- Can Redwood accommodate a small "surge credit" bucket that applies when monthly usage spikes above committed tokens? We want credits that the customer can consume automatically for the first 10% overcommit before overage billing.
- How would channel margin work if our reseller (ResellCo) is involved? They want a predictable margin and prefer credits to flow through them (escrow/credit-back) rather than direct patches on invoices.

Attached is our rough BOM with expected monthly token profile and addon mix. Could you outline feasible pricing approaches and how the reseller netback would be handled operationally?

Thanks — would appreciate a short call this week if useful.

Tim
Cobalt Analytics
Attachments: Cobalt_BOM_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Tim Jones <tim.jones@cobaltanalyics.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com; naomi.feldman@redwood.com; irene.choi@redwood.com; susan.kim@resellco.com
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GCP private offer question — bundled addon + surge credits

Tim — appreciate the BOM and clear asks. High level options we can support for the pilot:

1) Embedded surge-credit bucket inside the private offer: we reserve an internal 10% buffer that consumes a lower-priced token credit before triggering overage. Billing: private-offer invoice shows usage, but netback to ResellCo handled as a post-invoice settlement.

2) Escrowed credit flow via reseller (what you're describing): private offer mints credits that are held by Redwood on behalf of ResellCo; when customer consumes surge credits we issue a credit note to the reseller and route the settlement through the reseller's invoicing flow. This preserves the reseller margin but adds a short reconciliation step.

3) Hybrid: automatic first 5% as an in-contract buffer, additional 5% flows through reseller escrow.

I'll loop Ben and Naomi for margin math and ops constraints. If ResellCo (Susan) is OK with an escrow settlement cadence (monthly netting), we can prototype option 2.

Suggested next step: I'll draft a short private offer that pins list prices and the three options so we can agree on a single path to put into DocuSign.

—Rafael
Senior Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: naomi.feldman@redwood.com; irene.choi@redwood.com; tim.jones@cobaltanalyics.com; susan.kim@resellco.com
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GCP private offer question — bundled addon + surge credits

Quick math and practical constraints from a pricing perspective:

- Baseline list-price (GCP region): $0.12 / tok-equivalent
- Cobalt target private-offer effective price: 25–30% off list (they sign up for a 12-month commit)
- Reseller requested margin: 12–18% of list (or of net?) — typical ask is on net; ResellCo prefers margin on final invoiced amount.

If we do escrowed credits, operationally we treat surge credits as zero-invoice line items that are tracked and then show up as a monthly settlement to ResellCo. Proposed numbers (example):
- List: $0.12/tok -> private-offer price charged to customer: $0.09/tok (25% off)
- Reseller margin: 15% on customer invoice -> $0.0135/tok to ResellCo (paid via settlement)
- Surge credit: when customer consumes a surge credit token, we record internal usage at $0.09 but we release a credit memo to ResellCo to preserve their margin on the credit redemption.

Downside: escrow route increases month-end reconciliation by ~2–3 business days. Upside: preserves simple reseller margin math and avoids invoice rebills for the customer.

My ask to Naomi: can we do monthly settlement CSV exported to reseller with the following fields: invoice_period, token_type, consumed_credits, credit_value, reseller_margin, settlement_amount? Naomi — can you confirm platform support and whether taxes apply at settlement or on the customer invoice?

Ben
Senior Account Executive

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>; Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.com; tim.jones@cobaltanalyics.com; susan.kim@resellco.com
Date: Thu, 5 Aug 2027 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GCP private offer question — bundled addon + surge credits

Thanks Ben — ops confirms we can produce the monthly settlement CSV with those fields. A few notes:

- Draft private offer attached (Draft_PrivateOffer_GCP.pdf). It contains a billing appendix where surge credits are listed as a distinct SKU with internal credit tracking IDs.
- Taxes: customer invoice will include applicable VAT/state tax. Settlements to reseller will be gross amounts; reseller is responsible for their VAT handling (we'll include gross-to-net columns).
- Timing: to keep month-end tidy, settlements would be generated on day+7 of close window; ResellCo needs to confirm they accept that cadence.
- Accounting treatment: we can issue a credit memo for consumed surge credits and then a matching settlement payment to ResellCo. For audit purposes we'll keep CSV + signed private offer in the deal folder.

Action items:
- Rafael: confirm which of the three option flows Cobalt prefers.
- Susan (ResellCo): confirm escrow settlement cadence (monthly day+7) and acceptance of gross settlement amounts.

Naomi
Revenue Operations
Attachments: Draft_PrivateOffer_GCP.pdf (pdf)

Tim / Susan — quick summary and proposed next steps so we can get this into signature: 

Summary:
- We propose option 2 (escrowed credit flow) for the pilot: 10% surge bucket that gets tracked as a distinct SKU. Customer pays the private-offer invoice at the agreed private price (example: $0.09/tok). When surge credits are consumed, Redwood generates a credit memo and issues a monthly settlement to ResellCo that preserves their 15% margin on the redeemed value.

Operational details:
- Settlement cadence: monthly, day+7 after period close. Naomi will provide CSV exports and one credit memo per settlement.
- Taxes: customer invoice taxed where applicable; settlements are gross and ResellCo handles their tax reporting.
- Contract: I'll push the Draft_PrivateOffer_GCP.pdf to DocuSign with the escrow clause and settlement appendix. Link: https://www.docusign.com/templates/abc123-sign

Please confirm: 1) Cobalt OK to proceed with escrow settlement; 2) ResellCo (Susan) confirms monthly day+7 cadence. If both agree I will send the DocuSign for signature and loop in legal for the escrow appendix.

Thanks — Rafael
Senior Sales, Redwood Inference
